parsed.why: State-imposed facility and custody exposures: strip-searches by birth sex, sex-at-birth prison segregation, ward exclusion with a documented death, and a hostile single-sex-space code. No trans criminalisation and some protections keep it above Severe.

No criminalisation and legal recognition, but martial-law border stops of male-marker holders are a current outing/detention exposure. Recent trans-specific violence is scarce and dated; war and unresolved mobilisation add uncertainty.

Strong statutory protections, self-ID, hate-crime coverage and a prosecuted trans murder; no traveller-facing bans. High resident-reported violence and uneven service enforcement temper the score, but legal recourse operates.

Documented death sentences and mass punishments for same-sex conduct, modesty laws reaching presentation, militia and vigilante enforcement, and no state protection. Outing risks catastrophic state or private violence.

Decriminalised and little open persecution, but no legal recognition, police dismiss anti-trans violence citing male markers, impunity, and reported fourfold assault risk. Thin recourse places it in Elevated Risk.
